title: Sunday · Cedar, i · the gate
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: The first of twelve. The mill's gate, and the chain-link has grown into a hedge — the wire become branches, the padlock still a padlock. Played straight. The phantom novel bleeding through.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the mill's gate from the road, but the chain-link is cedar now — the wire diamonds grown into living branch-work, needles, cones — and the padlock hangs in the middle of it, real, rusted, locked.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, a mill gate where the chain-link fence has become living cedar branches woven in the same diamond pattern, a real rusted padlock hanging in the middle, played completely straight, no words
image.notes: The chain stays real (see dw_2016-07-24). Magic in the wood, not the metal.

panels.name: The gate

panels.composition: Tier 2: the padlock, close. Rust. A key-shaped hole. A cedar shoot growing out of the keyhole.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, close-up of a rusted padlock with a small cedar shoot growing out of its keyhole, no words

panels.name: Keyhole

panels.composition: Tier 3: through the gate: the yard, and the stack, with — this first Sunday — one branch out of its top. Held.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, a mill yard seen through a gate with a tall brick smokestack from whose top a single cedar branch grows, no words

panels.name: One branch

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: Cedar i. The gate grown. One branch from the stack.
